Documentation section docs/exporting.md#Exporting > JSON:

`write_json(books, path)` writes a list of objects with `title`, `author`,
`isbn` and `year` keys, indented by two spaces so that the file reads well in a
diff.

The chunk bookshelf/exporter.py::write_json before the change:

def write_json(books, path, indent=2):
    payload = [{'title': book.title, 'author': book.author, 'isbn': book.isbn, 'year': book.year} for book in books]
    with open(path, 'w') as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, indent=indent)

And after it:

def write_json(books, destination, indent=2):
    payload = [{'title': book.title, 'author': book.author, 'isbn': book.isbn, 'year': book.year} for book in books]
    with open(destination, 'w') as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, indent=indent)

What the change made wrong: The function no longer takes a parameter named `path`; it now uses `destination`, so the documented call signature is outdated.
